question:
Consider the determinant $D=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\2 & 3 & 1\\3 & 1 & \lambda\end{vmatrix}$.

(a) Expand the determinant and express $D$ in terms of $\lambda$.

(b) Determine the value of $\lambda$ for which $D=0$.

(c) Using the value obtained in part (b), verify the result by expanding the determinant along the third column.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=1\begin{vmatrix}3 & 1\\1 & \lambda\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & \lambda\end{vmatrix}+3\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3\\3 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=(3\lambda-1)-2(2\lambda-3)+3(2-9)$$
$$D=3\lambda-1-4\lambda+6-21=-\lambda-16$$

(b)
For $D=0$,
$$-\lambda-16=0$$
Therefore,
$$\lambda=-16$$

(c)
Substituting $\lambda=-16$ and expanding along the third column,
$$D=3\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3\\3 & 1\end{vmatrix}-1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2\\3 & 1\end{vmatrix}-16\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2\\2 & 3\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=3(2-9)-(1-6)-16(3-4)$$
$$D=-21+5+16=0$$
Hence, the value $\lambda=-16$ is verified.
